question.problem:
Suppose we would like to find the minimum of the function $f(x,y,z)=3xz+{y}^{2}$ on the intersection of the surfaces $x-y=1$ and $2{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+2{z}^{2}=4$ using the method of Lagrange multipliers. Then, the corresponding Lagrange multipliers $\lambda $ and $\mu $ satisfy the following system:  

$$
\{\begin{aligned}⟨\,\bbox[2pt,border:1pt solid black]{\phantom{AA}},\,2y,\,3x⟩=\lambda ⟨1,\,\bbox[2pt,border:1pt solid black]{\phantom{AA}},\,0\,⟩+\mu ⟨4x,\,2y,\,\bbox[2pt,border:1pt solid black]{\phantom{AA}}\,⟩ \\ x-y=1 \\ 2{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+2{z}^{2}=4\end{aligned}
$$

From left to right, what are the missing parts of the expressions?
